findings.title: U4 ISM6HG256XTR: JLC reports 9 in stock but only 2 orderable (canPresaleNumber), against 5 needed; the stock gate reads stockCount only

evidence.file: m3_design/assembly_review/fab/stock_check.json; tools/jlc_stock.py lines 116-128; docs/ORDERING.md section 8.1 U4 row; docs/REQUIREMENTS.md M1
evidence.measured: JLC selectSmtComponentList exact-code query 2026-10-31T09:54-09:57Z: stockCount 9, canPresaleNumber 2, minPurchaseNum 1, lossNumber 0; the round 19 probe (01:54Z) also had canPresaleNumber 2. Every other line has canPresaleNumber >= 2 x need (U9 45 / 29 for 5; C535146 201 / 194 for 40; U1 812 / 721 for 5). LCSC stock for C51931514 is 0, so JLC cannot be restocked from LCSC.
evidence.interpretation: Inference: the project itself reads canPresaleNumber as the orderable quantity (docs/ORDERING.md line 34 "stock 0, available -33"; docs/ROCKET_FC_FROZEN_DESIGN.md lines 29 and 63 "canPresale -519, oversold"). On that reading 7 of the 9 are already committed elsewhere and U4 is short by 3, not thin. JLC semantics not confirmed from a JLC document.

findings.impact: Procurement only, no hardware effect. The docs and the gate say "9 available for 5, buy at once"; if only 2 can be ordered, the order stalls at JLC parts matching or falls back to the LSM6DSV320X consignment path (CPL rotation regenerate, firmware register map), which ORDERING 8.1 already describes.
findings.concrete_fix: Record canPresaleNumber in jlc_stock.py and treat min(stockCount, canPresaleNumber) as available (fail short, warn thin); restate the U4 row in ORDERING 8.1 and REQUIREMENTS M1 as "9 in stock, 2 orderable"; on order day add U4 to the JLC cart first (or pre-buy into Parts Manager) and confirm the quantity before paying, else start the LSM6DSV320X consignment.
